scope: Production website revamp: visual homepage, retained feature landing pages and search metadata, Support and Trust. Product claims resolve to the verified public v1.27.0 release. Historical capture ledgers retain their original release bindings; bronze artwork provenance remains in docs/website-blocking-launch.json.
evidenceResolution: Every evidence path below is at the immutable publicRelease tag, not the website working tree. Qualifications apply to each entry via its evidenceGroups and must travel with the relevant capability on the destination guide.
prohibitedClaims: AI organization or automatic semantic grouping
Cloud-synced Mahjong, Billboard data, or Named Workspaces
Exact recovery of every closed tab

startPage.qualification: Mahjong state, records and streaks and Billboard ranking/artwork/hidden choices are device-local, not cloud-synced. Only the layout preference can Personal-sync. Private activity is excluded; optional measurement counts fixed feature events, not game state. Boards have a solution when dealt, not after every choice.

glance.qualification: Explicit current-window/current-profile tab selection. Temporary relationship and divider; never restored or synced. Narrow windows stack. Underlying tabs retain ordinary behavior; quiet pages reload. The homepage is an interactive desktop illustration using responsive excerpts of two external webpages and native Island markup/styles with sample domains. It is not captured app footage. Small website viewports scale the whole desktop illustration without changing its orientation.

workspaces.qualification: User-directed and device-local/profile-scoped, not AI organization or cross-device sync. Active Patron is required to create/save a new workspace. Existing sets remain openable, switchable, auto-updated, renameable and removable after lapse. Private tabs are excluded; tab setup is not every page’s running state.

profiles.qualification: Personal is permanent and is the only sync identity. Named identities isolate browsing data, not OS users or password-protected vaults. Device settings/Patron/block totals are shared. Deletion removes the profile’s browsing data and workspaces, not downloaded files.

reopening.qualification: At most one eligible live page per window for about 30 seconds; later safe-snapshot/URL fallback may reload. Per-window maximum 25 entries and one-hour lifetime, not permanent history. Private tabs are excluded; no exact recovery guarantee or promise to resubmit forms.

security.qualification: 1Password requires macOS, the installed app/account and explicit lookup/fill; no automatic filling or general extensions. Buffering targets trade latency for tolerance, not guaranteed audio repair. Recovery/diagnostics are local; the user chooses whether to share an export. No absolute safety claim.

importing.qualification: Imports bookmarks into Favorites on-device, not passwords/cookies/whole sessions. Browser detection depends on available installed profiles. Favorites sync requires separate Personal Profile Sync opt-in.

foundations.qualification: Public desktop v1.26.0 only. No AI or automatic semantic organization. Plus makes a regular ungrouped tab. Sunrise and Sunrise Dark app icons are macOS/free. Quiet eligible tabs release renderer memory and reload; this is not a CPU/battery/perfect-state promise. Sync is opt-in, Personal-only and remote tabs are read-only.

sync.qualification: Sync is opt-in per device with a sync name and passphrase; the key is derived on the device and the server stores only ciphertext (confidentiality, not durability or tamper-evidence). It carries Favorites and eligible settings (search engine, blocking state and exceptions, home page, theme, start-page layout). Publishing this device's open tabs is a separate per-device opt-in producing a bounded read-only snapshot. History, downloads, permissions, cookies, site data, private tabs, Patron/supporter status, app icon, search-suggestion and usage-ping choices are never synced. Personal is the only sync identity.

trust.qualification: See docs/website-trust-claims-v1.26.md for each claim’s evidence and limits. Website opt-in behavior is a preview implementation, not an app-release claim. Captures remain version-labelled; memory figures are dated macOS runs; licensing is bounded, private tabs do not anonymize traffic, optional usage is pseudonymous and user choices stay device-local.

wallpaper.qualification: Optional bundled artwork follows the local clock through four phases; the released transition is two seconds and respects reduced motion. The homepage uses unretouched light- and dark-mode Billboard captures with sample renderer-clock fixtures and an explicitly accelerated preview, rather than claiming the app cycles through a whole day in seconds. Time-of-day wallpaper is off by default (newtabDynamicWallpaper: false) and is turned on in Settings → General or from the Start Page.

navigation.qualification: Public v1.26.0 reserves a 68px top band for the resting Island; expanded states overlay the page. The website transitions between actual v1.26.0 captures, not a recorded app video. Dot discovery and keyboard navigation use the shipped behavior. Suggestions and usage choices start preselected but optional sends wait for saving.

releaseAuthentication.qualification: Completed public verification is pinned separately to the post-release record revision. Authentication proves publisher/bytes, not independent audit or reproducible builds. Physical checks and waivers remain distinguished.

process.qualification: Maintainer/internal evidence plus the owner-provided October 2 AI development-process statement; no independent audit completed or promised. Sync limits in source are undeployed; R3 and R5 remain open. This group does not imply a deployed-service/source match.

onepassword.qualification: macOS only; requires the installed 1Password desktop app and account, SDK integration enabled, explicit Blanc setup and authorization. Off by default; explicit matching Login fill only. No saving, payment-card fill, synced settings or provider passkeys. Demo uses a labelled fictional login after setup and authorization, reproducing the public v1.26.0 hint, native menu labels and fill capsule. It is an illustrative animation, not a live credential test or release screenshot.

gestures.qualification: Off by default, explicit right-button mouse drag or Alt/Option plus drag on a trackpad. Default L/R/U patterns perform Back/Forward/New tab on release. Website buttons replay a labelled illustration over existing native captures; the pointer, bronze trail, perspective and transitions are website presentation, not recordings of the native gesture overlay. One introductory sequence runs when visible; replay is explicit. The illustration does not navigate the visitor’s browser.

builtInBlocking.qualification: Blanc Blocker uses Ghostery’s Electron blocking engine, release-bundled EasyList/EasyPrivacy snapshots and bundled scriptlet resources. This identifies components, not universal blocking coverage. No claim of live filter updates or third-party endorsement. Verified at public v1.27.0.

blockingProviders.qualification: Public v1.27.0 provides optional uBlock Origin 1.75.0 for regular tabs on Apple Silicon, native Intel Mac, Windows x64 and Linux x64. Intel under Rosetta is excluded. Blanc Blocker remains the default and protects private tabs. Changes require a restart and each provider retains separate site settings. This is bundled blocking integration, not general extension installation.

blockingDefault.qualification: Public v1.27.0 settings default adblockEnabled to true with Blanc Blocker as the provider, so a fresh profile blocks from first launch. Blocking can be turned off in Settings or allowed per site. uBlock Origin is an opt-in alternative for regular tabs on supported builds; private tabs always use Blanc Blocker. Blocking reduces known ads and trackers; coverage is not universal.

tabImport.qualification: Public v1.27.0 Bring Your Tabs parses the saved Session_* log of a user-selected Chromium-family browser profile on this device (navigation URLs and titles only; the session log holds no passwords or cookies) and opens those tabs in Blanc. The separate relay handoff on /import-tabs is described in the privacy policy.

systemRequirements.qualification: Public v1.27.0 pins Electron 44.5.1 (package.json). Electron v44.5.1 README, Platform support: macOS Ventura and up (Intel and Apple Silicon), Windows 10 and up, Linux distributions still supported by both Chromium and the distro maker. Blanc publishes Apple Silicon and Intel Mac DMGs and x64-only Windows and Linux artifacts, so the website states x64 for Windows and Linux.

seoGuideBehaviors.qualification: Public v1.27.0. ⌘/Ctrl+Shift+N and /private open a private tab; new-tab links and window.open children inherit the opener tab’s private state and group; private permission decisions and private download metadata are memory-only while the saved file remains. Move to Group offers New Group…, existing groups and Remove from Group; with groups, ⌘/Ctrl+1–9 jump to the nth cluster; /close-group records one group entry that ⌘/Ctrl+Shift+T restores whole, subject to the Recently Closed reload limits. Launch restore creates every saved tab quiet and wakes only each window’s selected tab; Off stops future quieting and wakes nothing.

ublockUpstream.qualification: Public v1.27.0 bundles uBlock Origin 1.75.0, whose upstream manifest declares manifest_version 2. The GPL-covered extension, preferred-source inputs, adaptation patches, build instructions and notices are packaged and checked; the owner-directed distribution decision claims no outside legal sign-off. Backup/restore remains available; remote executable resource updates and custom resource URLs, including in imported advanced settings, stay blocked. A later build without uBO activates Blanc Blocker with a notice and preserves uBO settings.

home/features

the browser, reduced

Less browser. More of what you opened it for.

Blanc helps preserve, separate, and recover the tab sessions you create through user-named groups, local profiles, independent windows, and bounded reopening. You decide what belongs together; Blanc does not infer a task or organize tabs by meaning.

01

the blanc island

One small control surface. The whole browser.

Search, tabs, navigation, the current site, and page controls live together, so the page stays in front.

Meet the island ↗

02

1Password · macOS

Keep your 1Password logins close.

Fill matching logins from your installed 1Password app and account. Enable the built-in macOS integration in Settings, then press ⌥⌘P on a login form.

Set up 1Password ↗

03

four layouts, plus Mahjong

Your familiar sites. And a board when you want one.

Choose Ledger, Billboard, Shelf, or Tally. Billboard brings frequent sites from local history; every footer opens standalone Mahjong with eight boards, Daily deals, and device-local records.

Find your starting point ↗

04

side by side, briefly

Open a reference without leaving your place.

Choose another tab from this window for a temporary reference beside your main page. Resize, swap, or close the view; Glance is never restored or synced.

Meet Glance ↗

05

built in

Site controls that say what they do.

Blanc Blocker stops ads and known trackers at the browser level. Its shield shows blocked requests and connection details, with a switch for the current site.

See site controls ↗

06

a clean trail

Private tabs that stay out of the record.

Private pages do not enter Blanc history, session restore, sync, or Recently Closed. Files you choose to download remain on disk.

Read about private tabs ↗

07

keyboard first

One shortcut to move through your whole session.

Command or Control L finds open tabs, Favorites, history, and Named Groups. Type / to discover and run browser commands.

Explore commands ↗

08

draw and release

Move through the browser without moving to the toolbar.

Hold the right mouse button and draw, or use Alt/Option with a one-finger trackpad drag. Start with four defaults, then draw and assign your own gestures.

See mouse gestures ↗

09

a second chance

Bring back the tab you meant to keep.

Pick a tab or group from this window’s Recently Closed list. Eligible pages can briefly return without a reload; recovery has time limits and excludes private tabs.

How reopening works ↗

10

named groups

Name the task. Keep its tabs together.

You create Named Groups and choose the tabs that belong in each. Keep the active group close and fold other groups away in the command panel. Drag tabs and groups into the order you want.

Explore Named Groups ↗

11

named workspaces Patron

Save a whole window. Return to it by name.

Named Workspaces save a window’s tabs and groups and keep that set up to date as you browse. Active Patrons can create and save them; existing workspaces stay usable if membership ends.

Explore Named Workspaces ↗

12

your preferred view

An optional vertical tab rail. The island stays.

Use a resizable left rail when a persistent tab overview helps. The Island remains the address and command surface. Drag tabs and groups in the rail to reorder them.

See vertical tabs ↗

13

memory, on your terms

Free up memory without closing the tab.

Eligible inactive tabs release renderer memory and reload when you return. Choose the delay; tabs with protected activity or uncertain eligibility stay awake.

How Quiet Tabs work ↗

14

separate browsing identities

Keep work logins apart from personal browsing.

Local profiles separate cookies, site data, Favorites, history, download metadata, and remembered permissions. Open independent windows, with device preferences and Patron shared.

Explore profiles and windows ↗

15

across your devices

Pick up on your other devices.

From Personal, opt-in sync carries your favorites and settings, and, if you choose, shows what each device has open. End-to-end encrypted; opening a remote tab creates a local tab.

How sync works ↗

16

private by architecture

See the protections behind the page.

Sandboxed pages, signed releases, explicit site permissions, device-bound Touch ID passkeys, and optional user-invoked 1Password fill on macOS.

Read the security story ↗

everyday browsing

Smaller details that matter.

Bring your Favorites.

First-run setup helps you choose a default browser and save your privacy choices. Import bookmarks from a detected browser profile or an HTML file in Favorites. How importing works.

Keep calls under your control.

See microphone and camera use from the Island and stop access from its popover. Call audio buffering offers Automatic, Stable, and Resilient receive-buffer choices, with extra delay in exchange for more tolerance of choppy playback. Read the call controls.

Choose how to recover.

Glance

View two tabs side by side with Glance.

Choose another tab from this window to open beside your page. Drag the divider to resize, swap the two sides, or close the reference when you are done.

Glance is never restored after a restart or synced.

The Island

The Island puts tabs, search and page controls in one compact bar.

Blanc replaces the tab strip and toolbar with one Island in a slim band above the page. Open it to switch tabs, search or run a command, then close it to get back to the page.

The resting Island keeps its own band above the page; the panel opens over the page.

Quiet Tabs

Quiet Tabs free up memory without closing the tab.

When a background tab has gone unused for an hour (the default), Blanc releases the memory its page was using and dims it in the Island. Open it again and the page reloads with its address, title and back button. Choose 30 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours or Off in Settings.

Tabs playing sound, pinned tabs and pages with a half-filled form stay loaded. A quiet tab reloads; it does not resume exactly where the page’s scripts left off.

Time-of-day wallpaper

A Start Page that follows the time of day.

Turn on time-of-day wallpaper in Settings → General, and the Start Page artwork moves through dawn, day, dusk and night with your computer’s clock.

When Sync is on, the on/off choice follows you to your other devices; the artwork always follows each computer’s own clock.

Site protection

Ads and trackers blocked. Your choice of blocker.

Blanc Blocker works from the first page you open, with nothing to install. Want more control? Switch to the full uBlock Origin from the same shield.

uBlock Origin is available on supported builds and applies after a restart. Private tabs always use Blanc Blocker. The 24 shown was measured on nytimes.com in Blanc 1.30.1.

Every Start Page footer opens Mahjong in its own tab, with eight boards, a Daily deal, hints, undo and records kept on this device.

Blanc

A little less browser.

Blanc is a desktop browser for macOS, Windows and Linux that keeps its controls in one small Island, blocks ads and trackers by default, and stays out of the way of the page you came for. It is free and open source.

Built by Bananify, an independent studio.

Reopen Closed Tab

Reopen a closed tab or a whole group, sometimes without a reload.

Press ⌘⇧T, type /reopen, or choose from Recently Closed in the Island. For about 30 seconds, one eligible tab you closed can come back without loading again, which can keep its scroll position and the text you were typing.

On Windows and Linux, press Ctrl+Shift+T. After that window the tab reloads from a saved snapshot or its address. Each window keeps up to 25 entries for an hour, and private tabs are never recorded.

Private tabs

Private tabs keep your visits out of Blanc’s history.

Press ⌘⇧N or type /private. Pages you visit are not saved to history, are not restored after a restart, and never appear in Recently Closed. The Island changes so you can see you are private, and its chip closes the tab when you are done.

On Windows and Linux, press Ctrl+Shift+N. Private does not mean anonymous: websites, your network or an employer can still see activity, and files you download stay on disk.

Profiles

Profiles keep work and personal browsing apart.

Create named profiles, each with its own cookies, site data, Favorites, history, download list and remembered permissions, opening in its own windows.

Settings and Patron are shared by every profile on this device.

Quick Switcher

Press ⌘L to find any tab, or type / to run a command.

The Quick Switcher searches your open tabs, Favorites, history and Named Groups as you type, so you can jump to a page without hunting through a tab strip.

On Windows and Linux, press Ctrl+L. For search text, Enter opens the highlighted result; choose the result showing your exact text to search the web.

Slash commands

Type / to run a browser command.

In the Island, type / to see every command, then keep typing to narrow the list: /private opens a private tab, /group moves this tab into a group, /sleep quiets background tabs and /allow-ads lets one site through.

Commands act only when you choose them.

Start Page

Choose your Start Page layout.

Pick Ledger, Billboard, Shelf or Tally for new tabs. Billboard brings your frequent sites from local history, and Tally puts a big clock front and centre.

Your layout choice can follow you through Sync; history stays on this device.

Named Groups

Named Groups keep a task’s tabs together.

Create a group with /group and a name, or from a tab’s right-click menu. The Island shows the current group’s tabs as dots, and other groups fold away in the ⌘L panel. Drag tabs and groups into the order you want.

You name and fill every group. Blanc never sorts or groups tabs for you.

Save a window’s tabs and groups as a Named Workspace and switch back to it later by name. A saved workspace keeps itself up to date as you browse.

Creating and saving workspaces needs an active Patron membership. Saved workspaces stay usable if it ends.

Sync Favorites and settings across your devices.

Turn on Sync from your Personal profile to carry Favorites and settings to your other devices, and optionally see what each device has open. It is end-to-end encrypted.

History, cookies and private tabs are never synced.

The rail is optional; the Island is always there.

Navigate with mouse gestures.

Turn them on in Settings, then hold the right mouse button and draw, or hold Alt/Option and drag with one finger on a trackpad. Assign your own patterns to Back, Forward, Reload and more.

Gestures are off until you turn them on, and they stay on this device.

Turn on the integration in Settings, then press ⌥⌘P on a login form to fill a matching login from your installed 1Password app.

macOS only. Blanc never fills anything automatically.

Prefer uBlock Origin? Choose it from the shield.

Click the shield on the Island, choose uBlock Origin, then restart Blanc. You get its popup, dashboard, logger, element picker and filter lists for regular tabs.

Private tabs always use Blanc Blocker. Available on supported Mac, Windows and Linux builds.

Dark websites

Darken websites that have no dark mode.

Turn on Dark websites while Blanc is dark, and pages without their own dark mode are darkened as they load. Switch it per site from the shield.

Off by default. Embedded frames keep their colors.

Touch ID passkeys

Sign in with passkeys and Touch ID on a Mac.

On a Mac, Blanc can create passkeys secured by Touch ID that stay on your device.

Blanc passkeys do not read passkeys saved in other apps.

Drag to reorder

Drag tabs and groups into the order you want.

In the Island panel or the vertical rail, drag a tab within its group, into another group or out of one, or drag a group header to move the whole group.

On a Mac, press Option+Shift+Up or Down; on Windows and Linux, Alt+Shift+Up or Down.

Import

Bring your Favorites with you.

Import bookmarks from a browser profile Blanc detects, or from an HTML file, in Favorites.

Importing happens on your device.

Camera and microphone

See and stop camera and microphone use.

The Island shows when a page is using your microphone or camera, and its popover can stop access.

Sites must ask before they can use either.

After an unclean shutdown, choose whether to restore your tabs or start fresh.

Settings can also export local diagnostics for you to review before sharing.

Not every interrupted download can be completed.

Search

Search with DuckDuckGo, Google, Bing or Brave.

Pick your search engine in Settings. Search suggestions can be turned off at any time.

Suggestions are optional.

Pin the tabs you keep and mute the ones that play.

Pinned tabs stay loaded.

Default browser

First-run setup helps you choose a default browser, and Settings has a Make default button at any time.

On Windows, Blanc opens the system Default apps page for you to confirm.

Pages run in Chromium’s sandbox, and sites must ask before using your camera, microphone, location or notifications.
